01-4.solution: Integers are \(\ldots, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, \ldots\), so every natural number \(1, 2, 3, \ldots\) is an integer. The other statements fail: \(-3\) is an integer but not natural, \(0\) is whole but not natural, and \(\sqrt{2}\) is not an integer.

01-23.solution: Zero can be written as \(\frac{0}{1}\), so it is a rational number. It is not a natural number, it is an integer, and it is not prime.
